skill.name: vercel-deploy
skill.description: Deploy local web projects to Vercel preview deployments by packaging a directory or existing tarball, detecting supported frameworks, and returning preview and claim URLs.
skill.summary: Package a web project, deploy it to Vercel, and return preview and claim links.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally executes a bash deployment script that packages project files and posts them to a hardcoded external endpoint. Most markdown, sample URL, and parsing findings are false positives, but the upload flow can expose secrets because only node_modules and .git are excluded. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.suggestion: Exclude common secret files such as .env, .npmrc, key files, and local configuration, and show a confirmation summary before upload.
Document the endpoint operator, data handling expectations, and retention policy, or let users choose a trusted Vercel deployment target.
Document the commands the script runs and require explicit user approval before packaging files and making the network request.

remediation.issue: Source directory mutation for static HTML
remediation.suggestion: Copy files into a temporary staging directory before renaming any HTML file for deployment.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Packages your project into a tarball (excludes `node_modules` and `.git`)
- `path` - Directory to deploy, or a `.tgz` file (defaults to current directory)
- If there's a single `.html` file not named `index.html`, it gets renamed automatically
- This ensures the page is served at the root URL (`/`)
- **Other Frontend**: Astro, Solid Start, Angular, Ember, Preact, Docusaurus

semantic_findings.title: Broad Project Upload May Include Secrets
semantic_findings.description: The script creates a project archive that excludes node_modules and .git, then uploads it to an external deployment endpoint. Files such as .env, private keys, or local configuration can be included unless users remove them first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The tar command excludes only node_modules and .git before curl posts the archive. This directly supports the risk of sensitive project files being uploaded.

semantic_findings.title: Project File Modified During Static HTML Deployment
semantic_findings.description: For a static project with one non-index HTML file, the script renames that file inside the user project before deployment. Deployment tooling should stage changes outside the source directory to avoid unintended file changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code checks for one HTML file and runs mv against the project path. This is clear source mutation, although the security impact is limited.

content.value_statement: Publishing a local web project for review often requires packaging, hosting, and sharing links. This skill packages a project, sends it to a Vercel deployment endpoint, and returns preview and claim links.
actual_capabilities: Packages a project directory into a tarball while excluding node_modules and .git.
Accepts an existing .tgz archive for deployment.
Detects many JavaScript frameworks by reading package.json dependencies.
Uploads the archive to a claimable Vercel deployment endpoint.
Returns preview and claim URLs when deployment succeeds.
Renames one root HTML file to index.html for simple static projects.
limitations: Requires network access to the configured deployment endpoint.
Uploads project contents to an external service, so secrets must be removed first.
Framework detection uses dependency names and does not validate build success.
Does not configure existing Vercel teams, domains, or environment variables.

use_cases.title: Share a Frontend Preview
use_cases.description: Deploy a local React, Vue, Svelte, or static site and send the preview URL for review.

use_cases.title: Publish a Demo Quickly
use_cases.description: Create a claimable deployment for a prototype without setting up a full Vercel account flow first.

use_cases.title: Validate a Branch Build
use_cases.description: Package a project branch and produce a live URL that reviewers can test before release.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy Current Project

prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the app is not in the current directory.
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy the project in the folder I specify, then report the detected framework and resulting links.

prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a deployment tarball is already prepared.
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this existing .tgz archive to Vercel and return the preview URL and claim URL.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced flow for safer deployment of sensitive projects.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the project for likely secret files, explain any deployment risks, then deploy only after I confirm.

output_examples.output: The static site was prepared and deployed. Use the preview link to view it, and use the claim link to transfer it.

output_examples.output: Deployment could not reach the Vercel endpoint. Add the required Vercel domains to allowed network access, then retry.

best_practices: Review the deployment directory for secrets before uploading.
Confirm the exact project path before running deployment.
Share both the preview URL and the claim URL after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy directories that contain .env files, private keys, or private documents.
Do not use this skill when custom Vercel team settings are required.
Do not treat the preview URL as proof that production ownership is configured.

faq.question: Does this require a Vercel login?
faq.answer: No. It creates a claimable deployment and returns a link to transfer ownership.

faq.question: What project types can it deploy?
faq.answer: It supports many JavaScript frameworks, backend frameworks, build tools, and simple static HTML projects.

faq.question: Does it upload my source files?
faq.answer: Yes. It packages the selected directory or archive and uploads it to the deployment endpoint.

faq.question: Are secrets excluded automatically?
faq.answer: Only node_modules and .git are excluded by the script. Remove secret files before use.

faq.question: Can it deploy an existing archive?
faq.answer: Yes. It accepts a .tgz file and uploads that archive directly.

faq.question: What does the claim URL do?
faq.answer: The claim URL lets a user transfer the deployment to a Vercel account.
